**1. What we looked at**
We used daily prices from 2021-11-12 to 2026-11-12 (Yahoo Finance via the organizers' starter pack) and Bank of Canada USD/CAD rates. All returns are in CAD.

**2. What we found about you**
Mateo, you are 41 and want growth over 10 years with 150,000 $. You said you would hold through a 20% drop. You also said you would accept a loss of at most 25%. We used the more cautious of the two, which puts you at risk level 3 (Balanced). Your loss limit is 25.0%, i.e. 37,500 $. With a 10-year horizon, at least 38.5% stays defensive, so at most 62% can go to stocks. The caps are computed for you and for each asset; they are not fixed rules. Any single company (for example RY.TO or TD.TO) is capped at 12.3%, and crypto at 8.1%.

**3. Your request**
You made no specific requests. Your preferences (ESG screening, no fossil fuels) are reflected below.

**4. The strategies, compared**
Both are 60.0% growth and 40.0% defensive.
- **Broad core** (XIU.TO 30.0%, ESGV 30.0%, ZST.TO 20.0%, XBB.TO 20.0%): worst historical drop -13.9%, 2022 return -9.3% (stress test -12.9%), volatility 8.9%, chance of a loss 13.5%. ESGV takes the place of SPY to match your ESG preference.
- **Income / dividends** (largest holdings: XIU.TO 24.0%, XBB.TO 16.0%, AGG 12.0%, ZST.TO 12.0%, RY.TO 10.0%, TD.TO 6.5%): worst historical drop -10.3%, 2022 return -3.7% (stress test -9.3%), volatility 6.7%, chance of a loss 7.8%. ENB.TO is left out because you excluded fossil fuels.

In both cases the worst historical drop stayed inside your 25.0% loss limit.

**5. Limits of this analysis and what would change the answer**
These figures describe 2021-2026 only. They are not predictions or promises. The chance of a loss comes from a risk-only model. If your loss tolerance, horizon or financial situation changed, your limits and these strategies would change too. This compares options for you; it is not a recommendation to buy or sell.

Simulation only, for a fictional persona. Not financial advice; no real transactions.
